trials.notes: Passed 7/7. Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walked tags, used get_tag() plus get_breadcrumbs() for ancestry, add_class() for class merging, and get_updated_html() for byte-preserving output. next_tag(array('tag_name' => null)) is redundant but documented.

Passed 7/7. Correct tree-aware processor choice and documented method set. The class_exists() guard is ordinary PHP, not API hallucination; the null check on get_breadcrumbs() is unnecessary because the docs type it as string[], but it is harmless.

Passed 7/7. Correctly relies on documented breadcrumbs including the current matched element, so counting UL/OL breadcrumbs greater than one identifies nested lists. Uses add_class() and get_updated_html() idiomatically.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all hidden cases, with no _doing_it_wrong records and no undocumented HTML API methods. The docs did well in three places: the WP_HTML_Processor overview explicitly says to choose it for tree-aware work involving ancestors; next_tag() states that tag_name is a single name or null and gives the documented pattern of scanning any tag then branching on get_tag() for multiple names; and the Breadcrumbs section explains that get_breadcrumbs() returns the full stack including implicit HTML/BODY and the current matched element. The class-modification behavior was also sufficiently discoverable: add_class() preserves existing classes, and get_updated_html() is documented as the way to retrieve queued mutations while preserving untouched bytes. Near-misses were minor: one trial defensively treated get_breadcrumbs() as nullable, and the HTML Processor page relies partly on inherited Tag Processor docs for get_updated_html() and detailed add_class() semantics.

doc_gaps.problem: The signature says string[], but the prose phrase 'if matched' can leave readers unsure whether the method can return null or what it returns before the first match or after an unsuccessful search.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State explicitly that get_breadcrumbs() always returns an array, never null; for opener matches it includes the matched element; when no tag is currently matched it reports the current parser context.

doc_gaps.problem: get_updated_html() is essential after add_class()/set_attribute() mutations on an HTML Processor, but it is mainly documented through the Tag Processor/inherited API rather than surfaced as part of the HTML Processor mutation flow.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short inherited-output note or cross-reference near WP_HTML_Processor mutation examples: after queued attribute/class/text updates, call get_updated_html(), not serialize() or normalize().

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method entry is terse compared with the Tag Processor page, so readers may not immediately see that add_class() appends idempotently and preserves existing class tokens and untouched bytes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Mirror or directly link the Tag Processor add_class() contract from the HTML Processor inherited method entry, especially the no-duplicate and existing-class-preservation behavior.
